problems.title: The Moon
problems.statement: Determine (for the time of 1 minute after the beginning of your work at the round) and write down in the right boxes:

parts.statement: Astronomical azimuth of the Moon (assume the $0^{\circ}$ azimuth corresponds to South direction, and the counting is clockwise).
The height of the Moon above the horizon.
Constellation(s) in which the Moon is located (write the standard three-letter designation).
The angular distance between the Moon and $\alpha$ Cas (Shedir).

problems.title: α Peg (Markab)
problems.statement: You are provided with a small telescope (80EQ). (Focal length of the telescope: $F = 900\ \mathrm{mm}$; focal length of the eyepiece: $f = 20\ \mathrm{mm}$, and apparent field of view: $\mathrm{aFoV} \approx 40^{\circ}$). Target and center the telescope on a bright star Markab ($\alpha$ Peg), which magnitude is $2.5^m$. Then observe for the second bright star, HIP 114031, in the field of view (FoV).

parts.statement: Right is the FoV of the telescope. Plot the position of HIP 114031 relative to $\alpha$ Peg, and mark the directions by Latin letters N, S, E, W (North, South, East and West respectively).
Estimate the angular distance between these two stars.

answer.note: The source also prints 0.3333°; ±2′ earns 3 points.

figures.alt: Circular telescope field of view with eight dashed radial directions and a central dot labelled α Peg; directions and HIP 114031 are to be plotted.

solution.statement:
9. (points: 10(5/3/2))

9.1

Plot the correct distance (3 points), correct direction (2 points)

9.2, $0.3333^{\circ}$ ($20\prime$) (+- 2′: 3 points, +-5′: 2 points, +- 8′: 1 point)

9.3, 6.8 (+-1: 2 points, +-2: 1 point)
